ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, $OB$ and $OE$ are two rays within $\angle AOC$, $OD$ bisects $\angle AOB$, $\angle BOE=\frac{1}{2}\angle EOC$. Given $\angle DOE=55^\circ$ and $\angle AOC=150^\circ$, calculate the degree measure of $\angle EOC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle BOE = x^\circ$, then $\angle DOB = 55^\circ - x^\circ$,\\
since $\angle BOE = \frac{1}{2} \angle EOC$, we have $\angle EOC = 2x^\circ$,\\
as $OD$ bisects $\angle AOB$, we get $\angle AOB = 2\angle DOB$,\\
thus $2x + x + 2(55 - x) = 150$,\\
solving the equation gives $x = 40$,\\
hence $\angle EOC = 2x = \boxed{80^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the diagram, $OB$ and $OE$ are two rays within $\angle AOC$, $OD$ bisects $\angle AOB$, and $\angle BOE=\frac{1}{2}\angle EOC$. Given $\angle DOE=55^\circ$ and $\angle AOC=150^\circ$, calculate the degree measure of $\angle EOC$.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle BOE = x^\circ$, then $\angle DOB = 55^\circ - x^\circ$,\\ since $\angle BOE = \frac{1}{2} \angle EOC$, we have $\angle EOC = 2x^\circ$,\\ as $OD$ bisects $\angle AOB$, we get $\angle AOB = 2\angle DOB$,\\ thus $2x + x + 2(55 - x) = 150$,\\ solving the equation gives $x = 40$,\\ hence $\angle EOC = 2x = \boxed{80^\circ}$.

Image description: All rays in the figure start from point O; OA is a horizontal ray to the left; from OA upward, OD, OB, OE can be seen in order, and finally OC is in the upper right. Therefore, the order of the rays within ∠AOC is OA, OD, OB, OE, OC, and B is located within ∠DOE.

Reasoning: Let y = ∠EOC. It is known that ∠BOE = 1/2∠EOC, so ∠BOE = y/2. Also because ∠DOE = 55°, and B is within ∠DOE, ∠DOB = 55° - y/2. OD bisects ∠AOB, therefore ∠AOD = ∠DOB = 55° - y/2. The whole ∠AOC can be divided into ∠AOD + ∠DOE + ∠EOC, so (55 - y/2) + 55 + y = 150. Simplifying gives 110 + y/2 = 150, therefore y/2 = 40, y = 80. So ∠EOC = 80°.
